_comment: FLAT ground-truth solve of the 114-node fine clustered topology (no abstraction), the oracle for the hierarchical run. EXPENSIVE -- unlike TwoPodRail (30 nodes, deliberately sized so flat is cheap) this is ~96 sources x 600 directed links x 64 epochs = ~3.7M flow variables. Budget hours and a big-memory box; if it OOMs, that is the dense-flow-cube limit, and the hierarchical run is the answer you actually ship.
_expected: Host-uplink bound T* >= 0.880 s = 44 epochs, set by the 8-GPU hosts (704 GB across the host boundary / 800 GB/s of dual-plane egress). The spine cut is SLACK at 0.640 s, which is the whole point of a non-blocking fabric -- so LATENCY SHOULD TIE between clustered and scattered. The comparison lives in objective_type 5's switch-hop tie-breaker term: scattered puts 33.3% of cross-host GPU pairs on a shared leaf vs clustered's 22.6%, so scattered should show strictly FEWER leaf->spine hops at the same makespan. A latency DIFFERENCE means something is wrong (or an uplink got tapered). num_epochs is pinned to 64 (1.28 s of span, 45% headroom over the 0.880 s bound) instead of the default 100, purely to keep the variable count down.
_epoch_note: epoch_duration is PINNED to 0.02 s (= 1/50 GB/s, the fine GPU->leaf link) rather than derived, and this is load-bearing for the A/B. Derived SLOWEST_LINK sizing would give the two placements DIFFERENT epochs -- SLOWEST_LINK reads the MIN coarse capacity, which is 400 GB/s clustered vs 100 GB/s scattered -- a 4x difference in quantum, giving 0.0025 s vs 0.0100 s -- so the makespans would differ by epoch quantization rather than by placement quality. Same epoch on both sides is what makes the comparison mean anything.
_known_failure: The coarse LP can trip account_for_consume's 'assert consume == 0' on sub-feasibility-tol Gurobi flow noise (see the lp_extraction_feasibility_tol_noise note). feasibility_tol is tightened to 1e-6 here to make that less likely; if it still fires, that is the known extraction bug, not a topology problem.
_topology_note: The topology comes from the .topo DSL file (teccl/topologies/topology-dsl-frontend/examples/dual_plane_hetero.topo), not from the hand-written DualPlaneHeteroCluster class: topo_file SELECTS the topology, so TECCLSolver.get_topology builds a DslTopology from it and `name` is left as the free-form label the output filenames and Gurobi log are built from. The file is a verified port of the class -- same 114 node indices, same capacities, same ports/port order, same radix, same symmetry groups, same 8 cells -- so this input solves the same problem it did before, and the placement rule now lives in the .topo file rather than in DualPlaneHeteroCluster._gpu_leaf. The path is relative to the repo root, i.e. to the directory `teccl solve` runs from.
